analyst_view.overall: Early view: a meeting near the bottom, with Palace last after four straight league defeats and a 12-1 aggregate score in them. One report, from the Telegraph via Sports Mole, says Pierre Sage is on the brink and Thomas Frank is favourite to replace him, so Palace may have a new manager by kick-off. Jean-Philippe Mateta's three-match ban covers this game, and Coventry are missing Haji Wright and several defenders.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Palace have scored once in four league games and are without Mateta, which argues for fewer, but they have also conceded 12 in that run and Coventry will treat this as a game to attack. Those pull against each other, so I stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Coventry should have more of the ball at home, but Palace without Ismaila Sarr and Mateta have few outlets to pin Coventry back, and nothing in the news moves the total much.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards, which looks low for a game between 17th and 20th. I lean higher: points matter hugely for both, Palace may be under a new manager wanting a reaction, and a nervy relegation game is more likely to bring four bookings than two.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Palace expected to take 13.5. I lean lower: Palace have one goal in four league games and are without Mateta and Sarr, so their share looks high. Coventry's attack is also missing Haji Wright.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower for the same reasons: Palace's attack has produced one goal in four games, and Coventry are without their main striker, Wright.
